item.research_question: How does varying the Ti concentration (X = 0.3, 0.5, 0.7) in Ni1.5Co1.5CrFeTiX high entropy alloys affect their tensile properties, phase composition, and microstructure when processed via powder metallurgy?
item.material_system: Ni1.5Co1.5CrFeTiX alloys with X = 0.3, 0.5, and 0.7 (target atomic %: Ni28Co28Cr19Fe19Ti6, Ni27Co27Cr18Fe18Ti9, Ni26Co26Cr17Fe17Ti12)
item.processing_route: Mechanical alloying (dry milling for 35 h at 250 rpm, wet milling for 1 h in ethanol) followed by spark plasma sintering (1150 °C, 30 MPa, 10 min dwell) and annealing at 1100 °C for 24 h with water cooling
item.test_conditions: Room temperature tensile testing at a cross-head speed of 0.25 mm/min; microhardness testing with 100 g load (HV0.1)
key_findings: Annealed Ti0.7A alloy achieved an ultimate tensile strength of ~1680 MPa with a ductility of ~9%.
Annealed Ti0.5A alloy exhibited an ultimate tensile strength of ~1200 MPa and a ductility of ~14%.
Annealed Ti0.3A alloy showed the lowest strength (845 MPa UTS) and ductility (~2%) due to porosity-induced premature fracture.
Average porosity in Ti0.3A decreased from 3.77% after sintering to 0.43% after annealing.
Lattice parameter increased from 3.58 Å in Ti0.3A to 3.60 Å in Ti0.7A, correlating with increased Ti concentration.
Average oxide particle size increased from below 100 nm in sintered alloys to 150–175 nm in annealed alloys.
The highest strain hardening (Rm–Rp0.2) was observed in the strongest material, Ti0.7A.
item.mechanism: Ti increases strength by increasing the average atomic size misfit, thereby enhancing solid solution strengthening; however, high Ti concentrations also drive the formation of intermetallic phases (L12 or DO24) which are suppressed by the rapid cooling of the SPS process.
item.limitations: The study notes that the oxide contamination was significantly larger due to the use of ethanol wet-milling, and the precise chemical character of the oxides could not be measured precisely due to EDS resolution limits and signal contamination from the matrix.
item.future_work: The authors suggest that the oxides could be modified by adding elements with higher oxygen affinity (e.g., Y, Ce) to form more favorable and finer oxide dispersions, and that these alloys may serve as guidelines for designing inclusion-tolerant materials for sustainable metallurgy.
quotes: Ti increases the strength of the alloys by increasing the average atomic size misfit i.e., solid solution strengthening.
annealed Ni1,5Co1,5CrFeTi0.7 alloy possessed the ultimate tensile strength as high as ~1600 MPa at a tensile ductility of ~9%, despite the oxide contamination.
Despite the oxide formation, the mechanical properties were not significantly impeded.
